answer:
Hash a vector by the sign of its dot product with a random isotropic hyperplane normal. Restrict attention to the two-dimensional plane spanned by two nonzero vectors with angle $\theta$. The hyperplane separates them for a fraction $\theta/\pi$ of equally likely orientations, so a single sign bit agrees with probability $1-\theta/\pi$. [1](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

Concatenating $k$ independent sign bits makes exact bucket collision probability $(1-\theta/\pi)^k$. Multiple tables increase recall at extra memory/query cost, while probing nearby bit strings trades extra work for fewer tables. Normalize or use angular distance consistently, handle zero vectors separately, and benchmark against HNSW or other ANN methods. The single-bit formula is not the full retrieval recall: candidate budgets, table count, and reranking all affect end-to-end performance.
